![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14219165/assets/c1bf9d989f1fbaeda90325b924f2c9285cd4e37e1948ba63256258b0a84c7e44.png)

Find the arc length of the polar curve $r={2}^{\theta }$ for $0\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{2}$ (shown in blue in the diagram above).
questions.worked_solution:
The arc length $L$ of a polar curve $r=r(\theta )$ is given by

$$
L={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

Since $r={2}^{\theta },$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta }={2}^{\theta }\operatorname{ln}⁡2.
$$

Therefore, the arc length is

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{{({2}^{\theta })}^{2}+{({2}^{\theta }\operatorname{ln}⁡2)}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{{2}^{2\theta }+{2}^{2\theta }{ln}^{2}⁡2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{(1+{ln}^{2}⁡2){2}^{2\theta }}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\sqrt{1+{ln}^{2}⁡2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{2}^{\theta }\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\sqrt{1+{ln}^{2}⁡2}\cdot \frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\cdot {2}^{\theta }{|}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =\sqrt{1+{ln}^{2}⁡2}\cdot \frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\cdot ({2}^{\pi /2}-{2}^{0}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{1+{ln}^{2}⁡2}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}({2}^{\pi /2}-1).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Which of the following gives the arc length of the polar curve $r=1-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta $ for $0\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{4}?$
questions.worked_solution:
The arc length $L$ of a polar curve $r=r(\theta )$ is given by

$$
L={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

Since $r=1-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta }=-\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .
$$

Therefore, the arc length is

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\sqrt{(1-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2}+(-\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\sqrt{(1-2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )+{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\sqrt{1-2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +1}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\sqrt{2-2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }\,\text{d}\theta \,.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
The arc length $L$ of a polar curve $r=r(\theta )$ is given by

$$
L={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

Since $r=3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta }=3\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .
$$

Therefore, the arc length is

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{5\pi /6}\sqrt{{(3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )}^{2}+{(3\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{5\pi /6}\sqrt{9{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +9{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{5\pi /6}\sqrt{9}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{5\pi /6}3\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =3\theta \,{|}_{\pi /2}^{5\pi /6} \\  & =3(\frac{5\pi }{6}-\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

$L=$

questions.worked_solution:
The arc length $L$ of a polar curve $r=r(\theta )$ is given by

$$
L={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

Since $r=6{e}^{3\theta },$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta }=18{e}^{3\theta }.
$$

Therefore, the arc length is

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}\sqrt{{(6{e}^{3\theta })}^{2}+{(18{e}^{3\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}\sqrt{36{e}^{6\theta }+324{e}^{6\theta }}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}\sqrt{360{e}^{6\theta }}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =6\sqrt{10}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}{e}^{3\theta }\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =6\sqrt{10}{[\frac{1}{3}{e}^{3\theta }]}_{0}^{\pi /3} \\  & =2\sqrt{10}{[{e}^{3\theta }]}_{0}^{\pi /3} \\  & =2\sqrt{10}({e}^{\pi }-{e}^{0}) \\  & =2\sqrt{10}({e}^{\pi }-1).\end{aligned}
$$
